searchText: from the perspective of ZkEVMs ig you're correct maybe, but the main goal was to identify Zk-friendliness of verkle trie, since merkle uses hashing, and verkle replaces this with polynomial commitments, I think the question of Zk-friendliness of verkle might be answered if in the long run, we're able to find the answer to this question: is ("most-optimized")SNARK-friendly hash functions(for example GKR operations for reducing the cost of hash verification) is more efficient/cheap/fast than ("most-optimized")elliptic-curve-based SNARK(that address the problem of large field size, non-native arithmetic and curve operation costs for prover-verifier composition in verkle over banderwagon) ?, or simply existing SNARKified merkle vs SNARKified verkle for stateless clients, verkle might be one of the best choice, since potentially, in future SNARKifying verkle can reduce witness size to almost negligibly small
